items.title: Tom Malone interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 3, 2023
items.q: Bill’s good friend Danny Styles was the lead trumpet player in the band.

ctx.x: Well we did that frequently during the 70s and 80s. You know I basically played Saturday Night Live on the weekend and I did recording sessions all during the week. And I was in a group of people who were in demand. So people like Alan Rubin, Marvin Stamm, Lou Marini, George Young, the Brecker brothers — we would book stuff — we’d book a jingle from one to two and another jingle two to three. And we would usually get it done early because we knew we had another session. And that’s why they booked us, they knew…

in walking distance. So if we showed up ten minutes late we all showed up together and we got the job done. So even though that happened occasionally — I got into the business in New York — I met Bill Watrous early on and he would send me in to sub for him, to cover. I’d show up and I’d say, “Bill Watrous will be here in ten minutes,” and I’d play until he got there. And that’s the way I established myself in the business. Yeah. Bill Watrous and I became friends. I was playing trombone with a group called…

You just said something that I wanted to follow up on. The group of people that I graduated with, we all had aspirations to maybe get in a big band, oh my God if we could get in Buddy Rich’s big band. Most of them took the fall-back position and became public school teachers, which is an honorable, you know, position. But for those of you in that group that had aspirations to be jazz musicians, to have a band, to record for Blue Note, like your musical heroes did, but now you’re playing two, three, four sessions…
